In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HP-intake is associated with a transient worsening of IR in obese individuals, whereas HCF-diet improves IR in overweight participants.
the effects of isoenergetically increased dietary protein and cereal fiber intake on IR in overweight and obese participants are not consistent.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
isoenergetic diets with high cereal fiber content are more beneficial than diets with high protein content in overweight participants with IR.
the effect of dietary protein on IR is not a generalizable phenomenon.
the effects of dietary protein and fiber on BA metabolism are dependent on the degree of IR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
isoenergetic increases of dietary protein, but not dietary fiber content, may worsen IR in obese individuals.
isoenergetic dietary interventions that increase dietary protein and cereal fiber intake may be associated with adverse metabolic effects in obese participants.
the effects of protein and fiber intake on BA metabolism and insulin sensitivity are not the same in lean and obese participants, and that these effects are likely to be interrelated.
